question: What did Bolaji do before moving into data science?
draft: Before moving into data science, Bolaji built a strong foundation in statistics. He earned a Bachelor's degree in Statistics and Econometrics (2010-2013) and a Master's in Statistics with Distinction (2015-2018) at the University of Abomey-Calavi, focusing on statistical modeling, inference, and R programming. Concurrently, he worked as a Statistician at Le Pantagruel (August-October 2013), where he designed customer satisfaction surveys and deployed a scoring system.

documents.page_content:
Source: 01_career_overview.txt | Title: BOLAJI BALOGOUN - CAREER OVERVIEW & TIMELINE | Section: BOLAJI BALOGOUN - CAREER OVERVIEW & TIMELINE

EARLY CAREER: Statistician - Le Pantagruel (August 2013 - October 2013)
Bolaji designed and conducted a customer satisfaction survey with the Sales team, built a structured customer feedback database, and deployed a satisfaction scoring system. The findings informed management policies. Later initiatives were associated with an approximately 9-point increase in Net Promoter Score; causal lift is not established.

QUESTION: What did Bolaji do before moving into data science?
ANSWER: Before his data science career, Bolaji worked as a Statistician at Le Pantagruel in 2013 and at INStaD, Benin's national statistics institute, from September 2017 to February 2018. At Le Pantagruel he built a customer satisfaction scoring system. At INStaD he delivered hands-on R training and contributed to a national survey-funding data collection campaign covering four ministries. He moved into data science after a Big Data bootcamp at Rintio in 2018.

QUESTION: Que faisait Bolaji avant de passer a la data science ?
ANSWER: Avant sa carriere en data science, Bolaji a travaille comme Statistician chez Le Pantagruel en 2013 et a l'INStaD, l'institut national de la statistique du Benin, de septembre 2017 a fevrier 2018. Au Pantagruel, il a construit un systeme de scoring de satisfaction client. A l'INStaD, il a dispense une formation pratique en R et contribue a une collecte nationale de donnees sur le financement des enquetes dans quatre ministeres. Il est ensuite passe a la data science apres un bootcamp Big Data chez Rintio en 2018.

Source: 14_career_advice.txt | Title: BOLAJI BALOGOUN - CAREER ADVICE FOR ASPIRING DATA AND AI PROFESSIONALS | Section: HOW BOLAJI GOT INTO DATA AND AI: | Parent context: BOLAJI BALOGOUN - CAREER ADVICE FOR ASPIRING DATA AND AI PROFESSIONALS

Bolaji's foundation is in statistics. He earned a Bachelor's degree in Statistics and Econometrics (2010-2013) and a Master's in Statistics with Distinction (2015-2018, GPA 3.72) at the University of Abomey-Calavi in Benin. This gave him a rigorous grounding in statistical modeling, inference, survey design, and R programming, skills that still underpin his data work today.

The turning point was a deliberate career transition: right after his Master's, Bolaji enrolled in an intensive Big Data Development Bootcamp at Rintio (March-June 2018). This bootcamp covered data engineering and machine learning hands-on (Apache Spark, Hadoop, Hive, Python, SQL, ElasticSearch, Kibana, GitLab) through a real-world agricultural data project called "Duniya Data". It was the bridge from theoretical statistics to production data engineering and data science.

At Rintio, the March to June 2018 bootcamp was followed by production data science work on big data stacks and ML models. From there: Global Data Analyst at Gozem (2019), where he self-taught cloud engineering and migrated the company to GCP as its first data hire. Then Head of Data (2022), scaling the team, governance, and fintech-grade analytics. Then Data Director (2025), owning the data function end to end and co-leading AI strategy through July 2026. His path, a strong statistics foundation, an intensive bootcamp in big data engineering and ML, then rapid industry growth, shows that a deliberate transition works when you combine fundamentals with hands-on building under pressure.
